item.title: Online shopping takes charge as Dhaka’s malls fade
item.description:
There was a time when shoppers could be seen waiting outside several popular shopping malls in the capital even before the stores opened. Those days are gone.
Due to inflationary pressures, shifting consumer habits, and various other reasons, business at these shopping malls has hit a slump.
By contrast, sales at temporary sidewalk shops are booming. As people grow increasingly accustomed to a digital lifestyle, a significant portion of their shopping is now done via online pages. Under these circumstances, merchants at major shopping malls are growing anxious.
Recently, the long-standing, upscale Karnaphuli Garden City in the capital’s Shantinagar area closed down due to a lack of customers. This stately shopping mall once drew large crowds.
Merchants at the market said they first began losing customers during the construction of the nearby flyover due to traffic congestion.
Those who shifted to other shopping malls never returned.
Lately, things had deteriorated to the point where hardly anyone even came by to browse or bargain.
Traders at iconic, once-bustling shopping hubs like Eastern Plaza and Rapa Plaza report similar struggles.
Baki Billah Osmani, general secretary of the Karnaphuli Garden City Shop Owners' Co-operative Society, told Dhaka Tribune: "This didn’t happen overnight. The situation has been gradually deteriorating over the past decade. It started with the Covid-19 pandemic. After that, the rise of online retail, a lack of product diversity, and increased competition took their toll."
According to the shop owners' association, the mall had 198 shops. By the time it closed, only 17 were operational.
Highlighting the extent of the crisis, Baki Billah Osmani mentioned that their monthly operating expense exceeds Tk15 lakh.
However, over the past six to eight months, monthly collections for service charges barely reached Tk1 lakh to Tk1.5 lakh. Outstanding dues for service charges and electricity bills have climbed to nearly Tk4 crore.
As a result, the owners decided to sell off the property. Discussions are currently underway with several entities, including hospitals, corporate firms, and banks.
Malls have multiplied, formats have shifted
Traders note that the proliferation of new shopping malls has fragmented the market.
Another reason for the decline in older locations is the lack of variety in products and services.
Newer, larger malls offer diverse goods alongside multi-brand outlets, food courts, and movie theaters under one roof.
Consumers who have grown accustomed to these conveniences now prefer one-stop destinations.
Older shopping malls lack these amenities, causing them to lose their customer base.
This shift is echoed by Moghbazar resident Ziaul Islam, who said: "There are several shopping malls in this area, like Mouchak and Fortune. But if you buy a shirt from a shop here, you might not find a matching pair of pants. If I manage to buy shoes for the kids, I can't find other household necessities. These markets have no play areas or attractions for children. So now, I either shop online or go to Jamuna Future Park or Bashundhara City."
According to merchants, the rise of new shopping malls, brand outlets, and supershops in various neighborhoods has also reduced the habit of traveling across town to shop. Previously, people not only from different parts of Dhaka, but also from cities like Chittagong, Rajshahi, or Mymensingh, would flock to malls like Karnaphuli Garden City, Mouchak, or Eastern Plaza for festival shopping.
Helal Uddin, president of the Bangladesh Shop Owners' Association, told Dhaka Tribune: "One of the main reasons for the shortage of shoppers in malls is falling incomes. When people don't have money in hand, they cut back on shopping. Furthermore, more shopping malls have been built in the country than necessary, intensifying competition among store owners."
Helal places less emphasis on the impact of online shopping. In his view, if people have money, they will spend it. Without sufficient income to spend, shopping won't pick up through any medium—whether online or in person.
Online-driven businesses on the rise
Traders report that the expansion of e-commerce is transforming business models. Even as foot traffic in shopping malls dwindles, many retail stores are transitioning to online order-based operations.
Their showrooms now serve primarily as inventory warehouses and display areas for customers to inspect products.
SM Ekramul Hoque, general manager and office secretary of the E-Commerce Association of Bangladesh (e-CAB), stated: "Online shopping is growing steadily and will continue to expand in the future. Shopping at physical malls requires a lot of time. The opportunity to save that time is driving interest toward online channels."
However, e-CAB could not provide reliable statistics on the exact volume of online retail growth, making it difficult to measure the precise impact of e-commerce alone on the decline of physical shopping malls.
The e-CAB GM explained that many online businesses are not registered members of the association, making it hard to pinpoint the true size of the online market.
Nevertheless, he noted, a shift in consumer shopping habits is clearly evident.
A visit to New Market, Mouchak, and the surroundings of Jamuna Future Park reveals sparse crowds inside the malls.
However, the temporary street stalls and van-based mobile markets outside are bustling with shoppers.
These roadside setups sell a wide array of daily necessities, ranging from apparel and shoes to bags. Large numbers of buyers crowd these stalls to bargain for relatively cheaper goods.
Having learned through hard experience, Baki Billah, general secretary of the Karnaphuli Garden City Shop Owners' Co-operative Society, has advice for others: "All traders, big or small, must keep pace with the times. They need to focus on online sales and diversify their product offerings. Otherwise, survival won't be possible."

item.title: Bomb blasts, bus arson keep Dhaka on edge
item.description:
A fresh wave of crude bomb explosions and bus arson attacks swept across Dhaka on Monday, targeting areas near educational institutions, court premises and busy transport hubs, as the capital continued to reel from several days of violence that have left residents increasingly concerned about public safety.
The latest incidents came barely a day after explosions rocked Dhaka University, police facilities and other locations across the city, while buses were set ablaze in the capital and its outskirts.
On Monday evening, unidentified assailants set fire to a bus beneath the Farmgate metro rail station, prompting police to strengthen security in the area.
Tejgaon Police Station Officer-in-Charge Moniruzzaman said police rushed to the scene after receiving information about the fire and were working to identify and arrest those responsible.
Crude bomb explosions were also reported near the Teacher-Student Centre of Dhaka University and outside the District Judge Court, where suspects were detained in connection with the incidents.
In one such incident, a crude bomb exploded at the main gate of Government Bangla College in Mirpur, Dhaka, on the evening, while several shops beside the gate were set on fire.
In separate incidents, a bus was set on fire in the capital’s Pallabi area, while a van carrying gas cylinders was torched on Postogola Bridge in South Keraniganj on the evening.
Another explosion was reported in Shyampur, while separate blasts occurred near Shanto-Mariam University, World University and Southeast University.
Earlier in the day, explosions were reported near Titumir College and in the Rampura-Banasree area, indicating that the incidents were continuing from morning into the evening.
The attacks followed a particularly turbulent Sunday, when crude bombs exploded at several locations across the Dhaka University campus, including the TSC area, while other incidents were reported near the Criminal Investigation Department headquarters in Malibagh and Pallabi Police Station.
A member of the Special Response Battalion was injured when a crude bomb was thrown into the Pallabi police station compound, reportedly from an adjacent flyover.
Another person was injured in an explosion in Mirpur-11.
Meanwhile, a school bus was set on fire in Bhatara, and two buses were torched in separate incidents in Savar and Dhamrai.
The repeated attacks have heightened concerns over the security of public transport, educational institutions and government establishments.
More than 50 crude bomb explosions and eight bus arson incidents had been reported across the capital and surrounding areas over several days.
The violence has continued despite arrests, the recovery of explosives and intensified police operations.
In several incidents, attackers reportedly arrived on motorcycles, threw crude bombs and escaped before law enforcement personnel could apprehend them.
Police have also been examining CCTV footage and monitoring the movement of suspected individuals.
The Dhaka Metropolitan Police believes the incidents are part of attempts to create panic and disrupt public order.
DMP Deputy Commissioner for Media and Public Relations Md Akhtar Hossain said police were investigating the attacks and had arrested several suspects, including individuals allegedly associated with banned organisations and their affiliated bodies.
He said additional patrols, surveillance and intelligence-led operations had been introduced to prevent further incidents.

item.title: Hasina seeks passport to return, govt insists on extradition
item.description:
Former prime minister Sheikh Hasina has formally sought a new Bangladeshi passport and national identity card to facilitate her planned return from India in December, but the government on Monday made clear that it wants her brought back through the extradition treaty rather than allowing her to return as a traveller.
The development, first reported by Reuters, marks Hasina’s first known formal communication with Bangladeshi authorities since she left for India following the mass uprising in August 2024.
While State Minister for Foreign Affairs Humaiun Kobir dismissed the application and insisted on extradition, Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed said the government was examining its authenticity, legal basis and procedural validity.
The International Crimes Tribunal’s chief prosecutor, meanwhile, described the move as a political stunt and questioned whether Hasina genuinely intended to return.
According to Reuters, lawyers from London-based Matrix Chambers sent a letter on Monday to Preeti Rahman, acting high commissioner at the Bangladesh High Commission in New Delhi.
The lawyers requested a new passport and NID for Hasina, citing the reported cancellation of her existing documents by Bangladesh’s interim government and other authorities.
They urged the mission to process the applications expeditiously, referring to her Bangladeshi nationality and obligations under international human rights instruments.
Hasina has previously told Reuters that she intends to return to Bangladesh in December and surrender before a court.
The former prime minister was sentenced to death in absentia by the International Crimes Tribunal in November 2025 over crimes against humanity committed during the crackdown on the 2024 student-led uprising.
She has denied the charges.
Responding to the development at the foreign ministry, State Minister Humaiun Kobir described Hasina’s application as “utterly ridiculous.”
He said Bangladesh would not issue an ordinary passport to facilitate the return of a fugitive convicted of serious crimes.
The state minister stressed that Bangladesh and India already had an extradition treaty and that Hasina’s return should be handled under that agreement.
“If she genuinely wants to return to Bangladesh, she should ask the Indian government to hand her over under the extradition treaty,” he said.
Kobir also criticised the British law firm representing Hasina, questioning the legal and ethical grounds for pursuing the application.
He acknowledged that individuals could engage lawyers and submit representations to authorities, but said doing so did not automatically establish entitlement to a passport.
According to media, diplomatic sources also questioned whether the application had been properly authorised, saying the email did not include a signed authorisation from Hasina.
The Bangladesh mission in Delhi forwarded the communication to the foreign ministry.
Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed adopted a more procedural position, saying the government was still verifying the reported application.
Speaking to reporters at the Secretariat, he said he had learned about the request through media reports but had not independently confirmed its authenticity.
The foreign and law ministries were examining whether the application had been submitted in accordance with the rules and whether Hasina was legally entitled to apply for the documents, he said.
The review would consider the relevant provisions of passport, citizenship and national identity laws.
Salahuddin reiterated that Bangladesh had already approached India through diplomatic channels seeking Hasina’s return under the bilateral extradition treaty.
He said the government would take the necessary steps after examining the legal issues.
International Crimes Tribunal Chief Prosecutor Md Aminul Islam dismissed the application as an attempt to generate political attention.
“Whatever Sheikh Hasina is doing now is a political stunt. She will not come back,” he told reporters at the tribunal.
He said a formal press conference would be held on Tuesday, November 10, to explain the prosecution’s position on Hasina’s reported willingness to surrender.
The prosecutor’s remarks came as the government continued its efforts to secure the former prime minister’s return to face the consequences of the tribunal’s verdict.

item.title: How Bangladeshis lose millions to traffickers every year
item.description:
The promise of earning Tk4-5 lakh a month in Italy drove five men from Chuadanga to sell their land, livestock, farming equipment and even their wives’ jewellery, while some also took loans from NGOs to finance their journeys.
But instead of reaching Europe, they ended up in a Libyan detention facility, where they were allegedly held hostage and tortured for 10 months before returning home.
Human traffickers are accused of extracting around Tk1.47 crore from the five families through recruitment fees and ransom demands. Although the men survived, they returned without their savings or assets and burdened with debt.
The victims, aged between 21 and over 50, are from Phulbogadi, Nimtala and Barogangni villages in Alamdanga Upazila of Chuadanga. They were identified as Zahid Hasan, Kamrul Islam, Zahidul Islam, Alif and Sabbir Ali.
Their families alleged that the men were lured by an offer arranged through Mohammad Ali House, whose representative promised them lucrative jobs in Italy. The proposed payment arrangement required half the money before departure and the rest after reaching Italy.
Instead, the men were taken through several countries to Libya. On arrival, their passports, mobile phones and visa documents were allegedly confiscated, and they were confined in a room with 57 others, cut off from outside communication.
The victims said they were taken to separate rooms and forced to call their families to demand additional money. Those who refused to comply were physically tortured.
Zahid, 50, said he had once owned a farm with 300 sheep and a tractor, having spent 12 years working in Kuwait. In November 2025, he sold his assets and paid Tk29 lakh to brokers in the hope of starting a new life in Italy.
“I was held in Libya for 10 months and subjected to inhuman torture. I returned alive, but the marks of abuse remain. I spend most of the day sleeping because of my illness. I have nothing left now,” he said.
Kamrul, 42, sold his 60-sheep farm and 12 cattle, took loans and leased out his land before paying Tk32 lakh. Zahidul, 21, paid Tk34 lakh, hoping to improve his family's financial condition. Neither reached Italy.
The Chuadanga cases are not isolated. More than 300 young men from several villages in Bhairab, Kishoreganj, reportedly remain trapped in Libyan detention centres after being promised passage to Italy.
Families said the men were taken through Mumbai, Saudi Arabia and Egypt before reaching Libya, where local brokers allegedly handed them over to international criminal networks. Ransoms of Tk25 lakh per person are reportedly being demanded for their release.
The families have called for urgent steps to bring their relatives home. They alleged that a local broker named Rajan had promised to take them to Italy within 15-20 days for Tk22 lakh each. The money was handed to his uncle Arif, but Rajan's house has since remained locked and his uncle has reportedly disappeared.
Two young men who recently returned after escaping a Libyan torture facility described being sold to criminal groups and subjected to severe beatings, including attacks with pistol butts.
According to the European Border and Coast Guard Agency, Frontex, Bangladeshis account for the largest group attempting to reach Italy through Libya and the Mediterranean route. Between 2009 and June 2026, around 110,000 Bangladeshis entered Europe through this irregular route, according to the agency's figures cited in the report.
While men are often lured with promises of jobs in Italy and routed through Libya, women are allegedly trafficked to the United Arab Emirates with offers of well-paid work in dance bars, beauty parlours, restaurants and domestic services.
In many cases, recruiters reportedly promise employment visas but send women on tourist or visit visas. Once in Dubai, their passports and phones are allegedly seized, and they are confined in hotels or apartments.
Traffickers then impose fabricated debts of $10,000-$15,000 for travel and visa expenses, forcing some women into commercial sex or labour exploitation to repay the money, according to the report.
Allegations have also surfaced that some airport employees and officials facilitate trafficking through a practice known as “body contract”, in which brokers allegedly pay Tk30,000-50,000 per passenger to help them pass immigration checks despite incomplete travel documents.
An immigration official, speaking on condition of anonymity, said traffickers sometimes used valid visas for one country before sending passengers elsewhere. He said it was difficult for immigration officers to know whether someone travelling on a tourist or Umrah visa intended to move on to another country.
He added that action would be taken against any officials found involved in such activities.
Shariful Hasan, associate director of BRAC Migration Programme, said arresting local brokers alone would not dismantle the trafficking networks.
“Authorities must trace where the money goes, including the ransom collected from victims held in Libya. This is an organised crime, and the entire network must be brought to justice,” he said.
He also urged prospective migrants to verify job offers and consult educated and reliable people before travelling abroad.
Superintendent of Police Md Sufi Ullah of the Criminal Investigation Department (CID) said the agency investigates trafficking cases directly or through shadow investigations. Victims who return home should file cases with local police so that the people and agencies involved can be brought to justice, he added.

item.title: 250 checkpoints across Dhaka after series of crude bomb blasts
item.description:
Dhaka Metropolitan Police (DMP) has launched an extensive security and search operation across the capital, setting up 250 checkpoints a day after a series of crude bomb explosions at multiple locations.
Additional police personnel have been deployed at major roads, intersections and other key locations to search motorcycles, CNG-run auto-rickshaws and private cars.
DMP Deputy Commissioner (Media) Aktar Hossain told reporters that police had arrested 15 people in connection with Sunday's explosions.
"Security across the capital has been strengthened, and search operations are underway," he said.
Checkpoints and searches are being conducted in Tejgaon, Mohakhali, Mirpur, Gabtoli, Jatrabari, Paltan, Shahbagh, Karwan Bazar, Badda, Rampura, Uttara and Bhatara, among other areas.
Rampura Police Station Officer-in-Charge Jahangir Hossain said a checkpoint had been set up in front of Bangladesh Television (BTV), where police were searching suspicious motorcycles, CNG-run auto-rickshaws and private cars.
He added that two people had been arrested following a crude bomb explosion on a road in Banasree on Monday morning.
Sher-e-Bangla Nagar Police Station OC Monirul Islam said searches were underway beneath the Agargaon metro station.
Ramna Division Deputy Commissioner Sheikh Zahidul Islam said security had been tightened and all police stations under the division had been instructed to conduct searches and set up checkpoints.
Tejgaon Division Deputy Commissioner Ibn-e-Mizan said officers-in-charge of all police stations had also been directed to establish checkpoints.
Police are conducting operations to arrest those responsible for setting off crude bombs and spreading panic, he added.
A series of crude bombs explosions has rocked different parts of the capital since Friday with police stations also being targeted.
On Sunday night, explosions were reported simultaneously at at least 15 locations, including areas under five police stations across Dhaka.
A school bus was also set on fire in front of Bhatara Police Station. Earlier, miscreants had set fire to a passenger bus in the same area.
On Saturday night, four to five crude bombs exploded in front of Jatrabari Police Station.
The repeated incidents, occurring from evening until midnight, have heightened anxiety among residents across the capital.

item.title: COP31 opens with leaders under pressure to tackle climate crisis
item.description:
The COP31 climate talks kicked off Monday with an early fight over money as the UN’s chief urged world leaders to “get serious” about tackling the crisis after a year of devastating weather extremes.
Antonio Guterres made his plea as thousands of participants descended on a sprawling expo centre in the Turkish Mediterranean city of Antalya for the UN’s annual two-week climate conference.
The summit comes after a year of punishing heatwaves in Europe, major wildfires in Indonesia and catastrophic floods in Nepal, with an exceptionally strong El Nino weather phenomenon fueling more climate chaos.
“We have entered a new age of climate extremes,” Guterres said in a statement.
The UN secretary-general urged leaders to “get serious by cutting emissions faster, accelerating a just transition from fossil fuels and delivering the finance and protection vulnerable countries need.”
The COP31 opening ceremony opened an hour-and-a-half late without explanation.
Negotiators had been locked in discussions late Sunday over demands by developing nations to include items on climate finance in the official agenda.
“This has already been a difficult start for COP31,” said Jasper Inventor, head of Greenpeace’s COP31 delegation.
Under UN climate agreements, developed countries, which are historically responsible for most greenhouse gas emissions, have provided financial support to help developing nations adapt to climate impacts and transition to cleaner energy. But poorer countries say the sums remain insufficient.
Inventor said developed countries took a “hard line” over whether to include a platform, agreed at COP30 in Brazil last year, aimed at discussing how wealthy nations should provide funds to developing nations.
A source familiar with the talks said the “climate finance work program” would be included in the agenda.
African countries had also pushed for the agenda to include the tripling of adaptation finance, which aims to help poorer nations pay for measures such as building sea walls or planting drought-resistant crops.
The source said there would be no separate agenda point on tripling of adaptation finance but that it would be discussed under other items.
A senior European Union official warned last week that there would be “no political will” for extra funding pledges at COP31.
Observers say few major breakthroughs are expected at COP31 as countries grapple with an oil price shock and geopolitical tensions fuelled by the US war with Iran and Russia’s conflict in Ukraine.
The long-term climate outlook is bleak: the United Nations warned in September that global temperatures were on course to exceed 1.5°C above pre-industrial levels, breaching the most ambitious threshold set by the Paris Agreement.
Turkiye is presiding over COP31, with Australia leading negotiations under an unusual arrangement that settled a dispute over who would host the conference but raised concerns over how it would work.
The two sides have celebrated their cooperation so far, with COP31 President Murat Kurum, who is also Turkiye’s environment minister, and Australian Climate Minister Chris Bowen raising their clasped hands above their heads to applause during the opening ceremony.
The partners have branded the summit as the “implementation COP,” focusing on turning commitments into concrete action after years of pledges and ambitious announcements.
“We know that delay carries one of the heaviest costs in climate action,” Kurum said.
Turkiye is inviting countries to join a voluntary “electrification” pledge to raise the share of global energy demand met by electricity from around 20% today to 35% by 2035.
But the initiative could become a source of friction.
The European Union has called for “clean” electrification, a term that could spark debate over the role of oil, gas and coal in the Turkish proposal.
Countries committed to transition away from fossil fuels in a landmark pact at COP28 in Dubai in 2023 but have struggled to agree on how to turn that pledge into action.
COP30 ended with a deal that made no explicit mention of fossil fuels after oil-producing countries opposed the language.
Instead, Brazil produced a voluntary “roadmap” with proposals for phasing out fossil fuels that each country can tailor to their circumstances.
President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva, who will be among leaders addressing COP31 later this week, was due to arrive late Monday, fresh from a re-election win that activists hailed as a victory for climate change.
But climate diplomacy is still missing a major player as climate-sceptic US President Donald Trump has not sent officials to COP31.
A US congressional delegation, however, will come to Antalya, with Democrats beaming after last week’s historic US midterm election win.

item.title: Bus set ablaze in Pallabi, gas cylinder-laden van torched in Keraniganj
item.description:
Miscreants set fire to a bus in the capital's Pallabi area and a gas cylinder-laden van on the Postogola Bridge in South Keraniganj on Monday evening.
The bus was set ablaze in the Mirpur-12 area around 9pm.
Pallabi police said officers were sent to the scene after receiving reports of the incident. Necessary action would be taken following an investigation.
Earlier in the evening, another bus was set on fire in the capital's Farmgate area.
Meanwhile, a gas cylinder-laden van parked on the Postogola Bridge in the Hasnabad area of South Keraniganj was set on fire around 6:40pm.
Police sources said the van was torched near the middle of the bridge, prompting the driver to flee the scene.
Firefighters from the Postogola Fire Service and police from South Keraniganj reached the spot around 7:10pm and brought the fire under control.
In a separate incident around the same time, a crude bomb was allegedly hurled at South Keraniganj Police Station. However, it did not explode.

item.title: Crude bomb explodes at Govt Bangla College gate
item.description:
A crude bomb exploded at the main gate of Government Bangla College in Mirpur, Dhaka, on Monday evening, while several shops beside the gate were set on fire.
Darus Salam police station Sub-Inspector Dulal Hossain said police were dispatched to the scene after receiving information about the incident in the evening.
No casualties were reported.
“We have started working to arrest those involved in the incident,” he said.

item.title: PM: Govt to establish six dedicated 100-bed hospitals for workers
item.description:
Prime Minister Tarique Rahman on Monday told parliament that the government would establish six dedicated 100-bed hospitals in major industrial areas to ensure proper healthcare services for workers.
“To ensure proper medical care for workers and the working class, the government has planned to construct six hospitals, each with a capacity of 100 beds,” he said, adding that the hospitals will initially be established in Dhaka’s Savar and Ashulia, Gazipur’s Tongi and Kaliakair, Narayanganj and Chittagong.
The hospitals would be dedicated exclusively to workers, the prime minister said while replying to a lawmaker's question in parliament. “The hospitals will be named and developed specifically as healthcare facilities for workers.”
Earlier, raising the issue on a point of order, BNP lawmaker Shamsur Rahman Simul Biswas urged the prime minister to inform the house whether the government had any specific plan to establish hospitals in labor-intensive areas to ensure healthcare services for workers and their families.
He said they had heard from the labor minister about the prime minister's interest in ensuring healthcare services for low-income productive citizens, particularly working people.
At this point, Deputy Speaker Barrister Barrister Kayser Kamal said the lawmaker had raised the question ahead of the prime minister's question-answer session scheduled for Wednesday, as Tarique would not be present in the House on that day.
Responding to the query, the prime minister said Bangladesh's energy sector had been made dependent on foreign sources during more than a decade of authoritarian rule, with the country becoming reliant on imports instead of utilizing its own mineral resources for the benefit of its people.
He said the country's industrial development had also been hampered by import-dependent policies that prevented domestic industries from growing naturally.
Tarique said the country's healthcare system had similarly been gradually weakened during the previous autocratic regime, particularly in rural areas, where healthcare facilities established under earlier democratic governments had also been destroyed.
He said the Leader of the Opposition had also expressed concern over the country's healthcare system during a recent parliament session.
The prime minister said it was evident that the healthcare system had been deliberately destroyed during the authoritarian regime, forcing people of Bangladesh to go to a particular foreign country to seek medical treatment.
He said the current government had been elected by the people's votes and was working for people from all classes and professions. “The government is also giving importance to healthcare services for workers,” he added.

item.title: November rain brings signs of winter to Dhaka
item.description:
Residents of Dhaka experienced rainfall after a prolonged dry spell as rain accompanied by lightning began in different parts of the capital around 7pm on Monday.
Rain was reported in several areas, including Panthapath, Farmgate, Green Road, Banglamotor, Kalabagan and Dhanmondi.
According to the Bangladesh Meteorological Department (BMD), rainfall is likely in different parts of the country over the next few days, potentially bringing a slight drop in both daytime and nighttime temperatures.
The fall in nighttime temperatures may intensify the feeling of winter, although winter conditions have so far been more noticeable in the northern region. The department said there is little possibility of winter having a significant impact on other parts of the country at this time.
In a forecast issued at 6pm on November 9 for the subsequent 12 hours, the BMD said a low-pressure area was persisting in its normal position over the southwest Bay of Bengal, with an extended portion reaching the northeast Bay of Bengal.
The forecast said rain or thundershowers may occur at some places in Barisal, Chittagong and Rangpur divisions, and at 1 or 2 places in Rajshahi, Dhaka, Mymensingh, Khulna and Sylhet divisions.
During this period, both daytime and nighttime temperatures across the country may fall slightly.
The lowest temperature recorded in the country on Monday was 15°C in Tetulia, while Dhaka recorded 25°C.

item.title: Home minister: Govt verifying reports of Hasina’s passport, NID applications
item.description:
The government is examining reports that former prime minister Sheikh Hasina has applied for a passport and a national identity card (NID) in New Delhi, Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed said on Monday.
“The authenticity of the reports has not yet been verified. The Ministry of Foreign Affairs and the Ministry of Law are looking into the matter,” he told reporters at the secretariat.
Asked about reports in international media that Hasina, a fugitive convicted of crimes, had applied for the documents, the minister said the two ministries were examining the matter.
He said the authorities would assess the legal basis of the applications, whether they had been submitted properly and whether Hasina was legally eligible to obtain the documents.
Relevant provisions of the Passport Act, the Citizenship Act and laws governing NIDs would also be reviewed before the government made any official statement, he added.
On efforts to bring Hasina back to Bangladesh, Salahuddin said the government had already approached the country where she is staying through diplomatic channels under the existing extradition treaty.
“We have sent a letter through the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, in accordance with the extradition treaty, requesting that the convicted fugitive be returned to Bangladesh in accordance with the law,” he said.
Asked about recent crude bomb explosions, attacks on establishments and bus arson in the capital, the minister alleged that ousted political forces were carrying out such attacks to create instability.
Police would take legal action against those involved and deal firmly with such activities, he added.

item.title: Dengue claims five more lives, 2,260 hospitalised
item.description:
Five people died of dengue and 2,260 others were hospitalised across the country in the 24 hours to 8am on Monday, according to the Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS).
With the latest fatalities, the country’s dengue death toll has risen to 466 this year.
Of the five deaths, three were reported in Dhaka, while Mymensingh and Barisal divisions recorded one each.
Since January 1, a total of 152,173 dengue patients have been admitted to hospitals nationwide. Of them, 145,593 have recovered.
Currently, 6,114 patients are receiving treatment at hospitals across the country.

item.title: Five MPs named to preside over parliament
item.description:
Five lawmakers have been nominated to the panel of chairpersons to conduct the fourth session of the 13th parliament.
Speaker Major (retd) Hafiz Uddin Ahmed announced their names at the opening sitting of the session, which began at 3:30pm on Monday. The speaker chaired the sitting.
The nominated members are Md Shahjahan of Noakhali-4, Sarwar Jamal Nizam of Chittagong-12, Muhammad Naushad Zamir of Panchagarh-1, Shahjahan Chowdhury of Chittagong-15, and reserved-seat MP Rasheda Begum Hira.
Under the Rules of Procedure of Parliament, members of the panel of chairpersons will preside over sittings in the absence of the speaker and the deputy speaker.

item.title: ICT chief prosecutor: Hasina's request for passport, NID card a political stunt
item.description:
Describing the application filed by former Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina seeking a new passport and national identity card (NID) as a political stunt, Chief Prosecutor of the International Crimes Tribunal (ICT) Md Aminul Islam on Monday said she would never return to Bangladesh.
He came up with the information while talking to reporters, saying the prosecution would present its official position on the matter at a press conference on Tuesday.
Many media outlets carried reports that Hasina had applied for a new Bangladeshi passport and NID card through the Bangladesh High Commission in New Delhi, India, as part of her reported efforts to return home.
In a letter emailed to the Bangladesh High Commission in New Delhi, which was seen by the Associated Press, Hasina’s counsel urged the top diplomat to take necessary action to provide her with a passport and national identity card.
The letter, sent by London-based law firm Matrix Chambers, asked the mission for the application to be processed “expeditiously” on the basis of Hasina’s Bangladeshi nationality and in accordance with “obligations arising under international human rights instruments.”
Hasina fled to India after student-led protests had forced her from power on August 5, 2024 and had since then remained there.
In 2025, a Bangladeshi special tribunal sentenced her to death for crimes against humanity committed during the mass uprising, ruling that she had been responsible for ordering the crackdown, which left hundreds of people dead and thousands of others injured.
Bangladesh has repeatedly sought Hasina’s extradition, but India has declined to hand her over. She first announced in August her intention to return to Bangladesh in December.

item.title: Writ seeks ban on primary school admission tests
item.description:
A writ petition has been filed seeking a ban on all forms of admission tests for primary school classes from Grade 2 to Grade 5, as well as on supplementary commercial textbooks not approved by the National Curriculum and Textbook Board (NCTB).
Lawyer Md Mahmudul Hasan Mamun filed the petition on Monday.
The respondents include the Cabinet secretary, the secretaries of the Secondary and Higher Education Division and the Ministry of Primary and Mass Education, the director general of the Directorate of Primary Education and the chairman of the NCTB.
The petition states that under the Primary Education (Compulsory) Act, 1990, every child has the legal right to unhindered admission to primary education. However, the government’s admission policy for students in government secondary schools subjects young children to competitive admission tests, which the petitioner claims contradicts the law and exceeds the government's legal authority.
It further argues that such tests create fear and cause mental distress among children.
The petition also alleges that educational institutions, in collusion with commercial publishers, are burdening students with supplementary textbooks and guidebooks beyond those approved by the NCTB, in violation of the National Curriculum and Textbook Board Act, 2018.
According to the petition, the excessive academic burden and weight of these books can harm children's physical health, including potentially damaging their spines, while discouraging independent thinking during their formative years.
It also cites the National Education Policy, 2010, which provides for one year of government-approved pre-primary education. However, kindergartens and other educational institutions have introduced additional levels, including Play, Nursery, KG-1 and KG-2, without government approval, the petition says.
The petitioner argues that these practices violate government directives and turn early childhood education into a commercial enterprise.

item.title: German Business Council holds 3rd AGM
item.description:
The German Business Council Trust (GBC) convened its 3rd Annual General Meeting (AGM) and Members' Business Networking Dinner on Saturday, November 8, at the Gold Room of The Westin Dhaka.
The high-level corporate gathering brought together the founding trustees, and distinguished members of the German Bangladeshi commercial community to review organizational progress and foster strategic bilateral economic collaboration.
The proceedings commenced in the late afternoon with the formal 3rd AGM session.
During the meeting, the GBC chairman Md Zahidul Islam presented an overview of the council’s annual operational achievements, statutory compliance updates, and future initiatives aimed at strengthening trade ties between Germany and Bangladesh.
GBC members engaged in an open floor Q&A session to discuss key business strategies, trust frameworks, and upcoming industry partnerships.
Following the internal meeting, the GBC hosted an exclusive networking reception and networking dinner.
Dr Rüdiger Lotz, Ambassador of the Federal Republic of Germany to Bangladesh, attended as guest of honor.
In his keynote address, Lotz emphasized the expanding commercial synergy between Germany and Bangladesh, highlighting mutual opportunities in sustainability, trade expansion, and private sector investment.
The GBC chairman welcomed the ambassador, the board of trustees, and executive guests, reiterating the council’s commitment to serving as a vital platform for German businesses and local corporate stakeholders.
The evening concluded with an official group photograph, interactive business networking among attendees, and a dinner served at the Gold Room, followed by formal vote-of-thanks closing remarks.

item.title: Syed Tanvir Husain joins Banglalink as chief people officer
item.description:
Banglalink has appointed Syed Tanvir Husain as its chief people officer (CPO), further strengthening its leadership team as the company accelerates its transformation into a future-ready digital services organization.
He assumed the role on November 1, 2026, bringing more than three decades of diverse corporate experience, including over two decades in executive leadership positions.
A seasoned business and human resources leader, Tanvir brings extensive expertise in organizational transformation, strategic people management, leadership development, business growth, and workforce productivity.
Throughout his career, he has played pivotal roles in shaping organizational capabilities, driving transformation, and building high-performance cultures across telecommunications, technology, financial services, manufacturing, and diversified industries.
Prior to joining Banglalink, Tanvir served as divisional HR head – steel and consumer goods at Abul Khair Group.
Previously, he held the position of senior adviser at ACI Limited and served as chief growth officer at SSL Wireless, where he gained valuable experience in business strategy, growth, and digital transformation.
A significant chapter of his career was with Grameenphone, where he served as chief human resources officer for more than five years, contributing to the company's people strategy, leadership capabilities, and organizational transformation.
Earlier, he held senior leadership positions at Airtel Bangladesh as chief human resources officer, Citibank NA, and British American Tobacco Bangladesh, where he led the manufacturing HR function.
In his new role, Tanvir will spearhead Banglalink's people and organizational strategy, with a focus on strengthening leadership capabilities, accelerating talent development, enhancing workforce productivity, and fostering a high-performance, AI-first culture.
His leadership will be instrumental in building an agile, future-ready organization capable of supporting Banglalink's evolving business ambitions and sustainable growth.
Commenting on his appointment, Syed Tanvir Husain, CPO of Banglalink, said: "I am delighted to join Banglalink at such a defining stage of its journey. I believe meaningful transformation begins with people. By empowering our talent, strengthening leadership, and embracing AI as an enabler of productivity and innovation, we can build an organization that is agile, ambitious, and ready for the future. I look forward to working with my colleagues to foster a culture where people are inspired to challenge conventions, embrace change, and deliver exceptional business outcomes."
Banglalink welcomes Tanvir as its first chief people officer, reflecting the company's continued commitment to placing people, leadership, and organizational capability at the heart of its transformation.
His extensive cross-industry experience and proven leadership will play an important role in advancing Banglalink's ambition to become a leading digital services company.

item.title: Shahjalal Islami Bank holds financial inclusion workshop in Chuadanga
item.description:
Shahjalal Islami Bank PLC Organized a Seminar and Workshop on Financial Inclusion in Chuadanga on Sunday, November 8, at the premises of the non-governmental development organization 'Atmobishwash' on College Road of Chuadanga.
The program was cashless transactions via 'Bangla QR,' methods for small-scale and aspiring female entrepreneurs to access bank financing, and financial literacy and agricultural financing for farmers.
Managing director of Shahjalal Islami Bank PLC Mosleh Uddin Ahmed presided over in the program, while director of the Bangladesh Bank Rajshahi Office Md Nazim Uddin was present as chief guest.
Additional director of the Bangladesh Bank Rajshahi Office AKM Amirul Islam delivered a presentation on Bangla QR.
At the end of the event, agricultural financing cheques were formally handed over to the farmers.
Among others, head of the agriculture investment and sustainable finance department at Shahjalal Islami Bank PLC Md Abdur Rahim along with other officials were present at the program.
The program was moderated by Md Manzur Rahman, AVP of the bank’s sustainable finance department.

item.title: Dollar prices rise again after brief stability
item.description:
After remaining stable between Tk120 and Tk122 for a long time, the price of the US dollar has started rising again.
Within a span of a week, the price of each dollar to settle import liabilities has increased by nearly Tk1.
Currently, the interbank exchange rate stands at Tk124.35 per dollar.
In some cases, the rate for settling import letters of credit (LCs) has exceeded Tk124.90.
In the open market, buyers are having to shell out over Tk128 per dollar.
This market pressure has been generated due to the requirement of additional dollars to settle import liabilities for fuel oil, liquefied natural gas (LNG), and other commodities.
Although export and remittance earnings have increased against this backdrop, the supply of dollars is failing to keep pace with demand.
Data on foreign exchange transactions from Bangladesh Bank also reveals a widening gap between import and export earnings.
During the first three months (July–September) of the current FY27, merchandise import expenses reached $1.933 billion.
Compared to the corresponding period of the previous fiscal year, these expenses rose by 15.10%.
Conversely, export earnings grew by 7%. During this period, $1.186 billion came from exports, resulting in a trade deficit of $7.47 billion for the three months.
In the same period of the previous fiscal year, this deficit was $5.71 billion.
This means the trade deficit has increased by $1.76 billion within a year.
Petroleum products played the largest role behind this upward trend in import expenses.
In the first quarter, expenses for importing petroleum products exceeded $4.22 billion.
In the corresponding period of the previous fiscal year, expenses in this sector were less than $2.06 billion.
In other words, fuel import expenses have surged by more than 105% in a year.
Bankers stated that this expenditure has grown due to rising global oil prices and purchasing LNG at higher prices from the spot market. Additional dollars are also required to pay off LNG import liabilities.
Along with fuel, the import of essential commodities is also increasing pressure on the dollar market. In the first three months, expenses for consumer goods imports rose by 26.50%, costing the sector $1.40 billion.
Ahead of Ramadan, traders are preparing to open new LCs for items such as edible oil, sugar, lentils, and chickpeas.
Bankers apprehend that this will further drive up the demand for dollars.
On the other hand, capital machinery imports declined by 13.60%. This indicates that while spending on consumer goods and fuel is growing, imports of capital machinery related to production and investment are dropping.
Remedies
To increase the supply of dollars in the market, Bangladesh Bank is selling dollars from its reserves.
Last Wednesday, the central bank sold $120 million to commercial banks through an auction, with exchange rates ranging from Tk124.30 to Tk124.35 per dollar.
However, market pressure cannot be fully managed solely through the supply of dollars from reserves.
According to the latest figures, the country's total foreign exchange reserves have dropped to $34.85 billion.
Meanwhile, Bangladesh Bank has warned commercial banks regarding the rising trend in dollar prices.
Recently, during a meeting with the managing directors of banks, Governor Md Mostaqur Rahman stated that dollar prices should not rise to such an extent given that banks' net open position (NOP) remains positive.
He emphasized the need to remain vigilant so that no party can create instability in the market under the pretext of a crisis.
Arief Hossain Khan, executive director and spokesperson of Bangladesh Bank, told reporters that the central bank is examining whether coordinating institutions and bankers have any role beyond logical reasons behind the hike in dollar prices. Action will be taken if anyone's involvement is found.
Regarding the price hike of dollars in the open market, MS Zaman, president of the Money Changers Association of Bangladesh, said that dollar prices have increased everywhere, including banks.
A sudden surge in demand has caused some supply issues, but he hoped that the situation will normalize soon.

item.title: Consumers Forum: Essential goods prices rise by 4.39% in October
item.description:
Prices of essential commodities across the country increased by an average of 4.39% in October, driven largely by a sharp hike in fish and spice prices, according to findings by the Consumers Forum (CF).
Data compiled by the organization across various markets in Dhaka—including Karwan Bazar, Rampura, Meradia, Aftabnagar's Bhuiyan Bazar, and several super shops—showed that prices of 15 key categories of goods rose during the month.
Fish prices recorded the highest surge, jumping by an average of 11.72%.
Prices of spices, including cloves, cardamom, cinnamon, and cumin, rose by 10.30%, while onions, garlic, and ginger saw a 7.79% increase.
Other notable price hikes included fuel oil (6.02%), sugar (4.93%), edible oil and dalda (4.80%), flour and maida (3.25%), rice (2.62%), eggs (1.42%), meat (0.38%), and tea (0.14%).
Conversely, prices of seven essential items, including salt, dairy products, toothpaste, biscuits, 11 major brands of medicines, and stationery items, remained stable.
Meanwhile, prices dropped for two categories: vegetables fell by 3.12% and gold and silver by 4.77%.
Field reports from different parts of the vegetable supply hub, including Jessore, Bogra, and Rangpur, indicated that winter vegetables have begun arriving in local wholesale markets, though producers are struggling to recover their production costs.
While cauliflower and cabbage sold for Tk6–12, radishes for Tk6–8, gourds for Tk8–10, and plantains for Tk5–8 per 4-piece (hali) locally in regions like Bogra and Rangpur, they were retailed at much higher prices in Dhaka, with cauliflowers and cabbages fetching around Tk50, papayas and radishes Tk30, gourds Tk60, and plantains Tk40–50 per hali.
According to the Consumers Forum, essential commodity prices had already risen by 3.13% in September, bringing the cumulative two-month increase to 7.52%.
In a press release issued Sunday by CF General Secretary Emdad Hossain Malek, the organization emphasized that merely raising wages is insufficient.
It called on authorities to keep essential living expenses—including urban house and shop rents, education, and healthcare—within the purchasing power of middle and lower-middle-income groups.
The forum urged strict administrative and legal actions to curb excessive profit-seeking by unscrupulous traders and safeguard public welfare.

item.title: Crude bomb explosions at multiple locations in Gopalganj
item.description:
A series of crude bomb explosions at several key locations in Gopalganj on Monday night triggered panic among residents amid a programme called by a banned organisation.
Police have stepped up security across the district to prevent further incidents and maintain law and order.
According to local sources, crude bombs were detonated near the main gate of Gopalganj District School, along the boundary walls of the Government Women's College and passport office, and in front of the Government Technical School and College.
The blasts caused panic among residents in the surrounding areas.
In a separate incident, a crude bomb exploded beside the Upazila Muktijoddha Complex in Kotalipara at around 9:15pm. A group of miscreants arrived on motorcycles, detonated the bomb and fled the scene.
No casualties or damage were reported.
Kotalipara Fire Service Station Master Sirajul Islam confirmed the explosion, saying the bomb went off in an open space in front of the complex.
He said a generator at Café Ekattor, located behind the complex, caught fire shortly afterwards due to overheating. Fire service personnel rushed to the spot and brought the blaze under control. However, he clarified that there was no connection between the bomb explosion and the generator fire.
Law enforcement personnel rushed to the locations following the incidents. Police have increased patrols and tightened security across the district to prevent further disturbances.
No casualties have been reported in any of the incidents so far.

item.title: Crude bomb explodes at JnU, one suspect detained
item.description:
A crude bomb exploded in the parking area near the second gate of Jagannath University (JnU) on Monday evening, prompting the university's Chhatra Dal unit to detain a suspected individual.
The explosion occurred at around 7:30pm between two buses parked near the gate. The detainee was identified as Rezwan Ahmed, a student of the Department of Psychology from the 2021-22 academic session. Preliminary information suggests that he is an activist of the university's Chhatra League.
Eyewitnesses said they heard a loud bang at around 7:30pm, followed by smoke rising from the area. The blast occurred between two parked buses near the university's second gate.
However, no one was seen at the scene immediately after the explosion, they added.
University Proctor Professor Nasir Ahmad said they had heard about the explosion near the second gate while it was raining in the evening.
"We were not on campus at the time. We will review the CCTV footage to identify those involved," he said.
Regarding the detention, the proctor said the university's Chhatra Dal unit had detained a suspect and that they had contacted the police.

item.title: Six AL activists arrested while hurling crude bombs in Dhaka
item.description:
Dhaka Metropolitan Police (DMP) have arrested six activists of the banned Awami League and its affiliated organisations while they were allegedly hurling crude bombs in different parts of the capital. Three crude bombs and a motorcycle were recovered from their possession.
The DMP media division disclosed the information on Monday night.
A series of crude bombs explosions have rocked different parts of the capital over the past few days. Several explosions and incidents of bus arson were also reported at different locations on Monday.
Amid the spate of incidents, law enforcement agencies have tightened security across the capital.

item.title: Ahsan's 152, Tafiul’s 7-for steer Bangladesh U19s into Asia Cup semis
item.description:
Bangladesh Under-19 team stormed into the semifinals of the Under-19 Asia Cup with a crushing 205-run victory over Malaysia on Monday after Ahsan Al Mumin's unbeaten 152 and Tafiul Alam Tamim's seven-wicket haul today at Al Amerat Cricket Ground in Oman.
Bangladesh posted 303-8 in 50 overs after winning the toss and electing to bat, before bowling out Malaysia for just 98 in 30.5 overs.
Ahsan was the standout performer with the bat, smashing an unbeaten 152 off 133 balls, including 10 fours and six sixes.
Robiul Hasan Anik provided valuable support with 45 off 48 balls as Bangladesh recovered from an early setback to post a formidable total.
Malaysia's Nagineswaran Sathnakumaran, Syahir Asyraf and Aulga Gunawan claimed two wickets apiece.
In reply, Malaysia's batting line-up had no answer to Tafiul's devastating spell. The right-arm bowler claimed seven wickets for just 18 runs in 7.5 overs, including two maiden overs, to dismantle the opposition.
Nagineswaran offered some resistance with 50 off 81 balls but received little support from his teammates.
Rubay Islam Rizon complemented Tamim's effort with two wickets as Bangladesh completed a comprehensive victory to secure their semifinal berth. Their semifinal opponents are yet to be confirmed.

item.title: Bad light forces draw in Sylhet as West Indies take series
item.description:
Bad light ended the second Test between Bangladesh and West Indies in a draw in Sylhet on Monday, handing the visitors a 1-0 series win.
Bangladesh were 184 for four in their chase of 369 when bad light stopped play before 2:45pm on the final day. They still needed 185 runs, while West Indies needed six wickets.
The umpires were due to inspect the light at 4pm, but the two captains agreed to a draw before that. West Indies had won the first Test in Mirpur by eight wickets.
Towhid Hridoy, who scored an unbeaten 242 in the first innings, followed it with 82 and was named player of the match. He became the first Bangladesh batter to score a double century and a fifty in the same Test.
West Indies left-arm spinner Jomel Warrican was named player of the series for his 16 wickets, nine in the first Test and seven in the second.
West Indies resumed on 345 for three, added 53 runs in 10 overs and declared on 398 for six. Kavem Hodge made 142, his third Test century, while Kevin Wickham scored 78 and Brendon King 61.
Nayeem Hasan took two for 72, Mehidy Hasan Miraz two for 85 and Taijul Islam two for 118.
Bangladesh lost both openers before lunch. Tanzid Hasan was caught at the midwicket boundary for 21 trying to hit Warrican for six. Captain Najmul Hossain Shanto was given lbw for 14 off Warrican after a West Indies review, leaving Bangladesh on 40 for two.
Hridoy and Mushfiqur Rahim then batted through the entire second session without losing a wicket, adding 113 runs in 34 overs. Their third-wicket stand was worth 135 runs.
During the innings, Mushfiqur became the first Bangladesh batter to score 7,000 Test runs. He reached the mark with a single off Warrican in the 20th over. Mominul Haque is second on the list with 5,293 runs.
Bangladesh lost both set batters within the first nine overs after tea. Hridoy was bowled for 82 trying to sweep Warrican, missing a full delivery from over the wicket that pitched well outside leg stump. It was Warrican's 100th Test wicket.
Mushfiqur fell one short of his fifty when Shamar Joseph bowled him for 49 off 123 balls. Litton Das and Miraz were at the crease when the light faded.
"Apart from Hridoy, nobody batted well in the first innings, and we paid the price for that," Shanto said after the match.
Hridoy spoke about batting with Mushfiqur. "I've followed Mushi bhai since childhood. He is my idol, and I always try to learn from him," he said.
Bangladesh made 386 in their first innings in reply to West Indies' 356, with pacer Hasan Mahmud taking six for 90.
Bangladesh fly to South Africa on Tuesday for a two-Test series. The first Test begins in Johannesburg on November 15.

item.title: Hamza joins Bangladesh team for remaining SAFF fixtures
item.description:
Hamza Choudhury has arrived in Bangladesh on Monday to join the national team ahead of their remaining fixtures in the TECNO SAFF Championship 2026.
The Leicester City midfielder, currently on loan at English Championship side Sheffield United, was received by Bangladesh Football Federation (BFF) Executive Committee Member and Team Manager Amirul Islam Babu, along with BFF Executive Committee Member and National Teams Committee Member Imteaz Hamid Shobuj.
Hamza missed Bangladesh's opening Group A fixture against Bhutan as he was unable to join the squad earlier due to his club commitments in England, with the FIFA international window not yet open.
The midfielder's arrival is expected to provide a major boost to the Bangladesh side ahead of their second and final group match against Sri Lanka on Wednesday.
Bangladesh began their campaign with a 1-0 victory over Bhutan at the National Stadium in Dhaka on Thursday, with substitute Mohammad Ibrahim scoring the decisive goal in the 69th minute.
The men in red and green have already secured their place in the semi-finals after Bhutan and Sri Lanka played out a 2-2 draw in their Group A encounter on Sunday.
Bangladesh will now look to finish the group stage on a high, with a victory over Sri Lanka ensuring they advance to the knockouts as group winners.

item.title: Eric Mare named interim Bangladesh women’s team coach
item.description:
The Bangladesh Football Federation (BFF) on Monday appointed Eric Mare as interim head coach of the national women’s football team for a one-month assignment, with regular coach Peter Butler undergoing cancer treatment in England.
Mare will take charge of the team as the reigning SAFF champions prepare for their upcoming international commitments against Singapore, the BFF announced in a statement.
“The Bangladesh Football Federation (BFF) is pleased to announce the appointment of Mr. Eric Mare as the Interim Head Coach of the Bangladesh Women’s National Football Team for a one-month assignment,” the statement read.
The women’s team is currently training in a camp ahead of two friendly matches against Singapore on December 1 and 5.
Earlier on Sunday, Butler informed the media that he had been diagnosed with cancer. The English coach also revealed that the BFF had sought his permission to appoint an interim coach during his absence, which he granted.
Butler, however, expressed his determination to fight the disease and return to Bangladesh to resume his coaching duties.
Meanwhile, the BFF extended its best wishes to Butler for a speedy recovery.
“The BFF extends its heartfelt best wishes to Mr. Peter Butler, Head Coach of the Bangladesh Women’s National Team, for a speedy and full recovery. We sincerely hope he regains his health soon and rejoins the team,” the statement added.

item.title: Mushfiqur becomes first Bangladesh batter to score 7,000 Test runs
item.description:
Mushfiqur Rahim became the first Bangladeshi cricketer to reach 7,000 runs in Test cricket, achieving the milestone with a single off Roston Chase in the 20th over of Bangladesh’s second innings on the fifth day of their Test against the West Indies at Sylhet International Cricket Stadium on Monday.
Bangladesh were chasing 369 for victory, with Mushfiqur and Towhid Hridoy anchoring the innings in a third-wicket partnership.
Mushfiqur brought up the landmark with a single to mid-on off an angling length delivery from Chase, etching his name into the record books.
Bangladesh’s most-capped Test cricketer also holds the national record for the most Test centuries.
Mushfiqur, who missed the first Test of the series after sustaining a finger injury, was also the first Bangladesh batter to reach 5,000 and 6,000 runs in the longest format.
Mominul Haque and the now-retired Tamim Iqbal occupy the second and third positions behind Mushfiqur on Bangladesh’s all-time Test run-scoring list.
The two are also behind Mushfiqur among Bangladesh’s highest century-makers in Tests. Mushfiqur has 14 centuries, including a career-best 219 not out, which was the country’s highest individual Test score before Hridoy surpassed it with an unbeaten 242 earlier in the Sylhet Test.
Mominul and Tamim have 13 and 10 Test centuries respectively.
Having made his international debut in 2005, Mushfiqur is Bangladesh’s most experienced Test cricketer. He was playing his 107th Test, having become the first Bangladeshi to feature in 100 Tests in November 2025.
Mushfiqur was eventually bowled by Shamar Joseph for 49, narrowly missing out on his 31st Test half-century, as Bangladesh reached 183 for four in the 57th over.
