item.title: Jail Killing Day: Bangladesh remembers four national leaders
Dhaka Elevated Expressway to remain toll-free for six hours on Nov 7
item.description:
The Dhaka Elevated Expressway will remain toll-free for six hours on Saturday, marking National Revolution and Solidarity Day. All vehicles will be allowed to use the expressway free of charge from 6:00am to 12pm.
The Bangladesh Bridge Authority announced the decision in a press release on Tuesday.
According to the press release, the toll-free facility will apply to all vehicles using the expressway during the designated six-hour period.
Last year, the expressway was kept toll-free for four hours on December 25, when BNP Chairman and Prime Minister Tarique Rahman returned home from London after nearly 17 years. The BNP organised a public reception to mark his return.
The expressway also operated without toll collection for several days after toll plazas were damaged during the July Mass Uprising.
Built under a public-private partnership (PPP), the Dhaka Elevated Expressway was partially opened to traffic in September 2023. Currently, the operational section stretches from Kawla, near Hazrat Shahjalal International Airport, to the FDC intersection in the capital. Vehicles are normally charged tolls for using the expressway.
Toll rates vary by vehicle category. Cars, taxis, sports utility vehicles (SUVs), microbuses with fewer than 16 seats and light trucks weighing less than three tonnes are charged Tk80.
Medium trucks with up to six wheels are charged Tk320, while trucks with more than six wheels pay Tk400. Buses with 16 or more seats are charged Tk160.
Rickshaws, motorcycles and auto-rickshaws are not allowed on the expressway.
The 19.73-kilometre expressway is designed to connect Kawla, near Hazrat Shahjalal International Airport, with Kutubkhali near Jatrabari on the Dhaka-Chittagong Highway, passing through Tejgaon, Moghbazar and Kamalapur along the railway corridor.
However, construction of the full route is yet to be completed.
The project comprises two components: the main construction work and associated works.
The main construction component has an estimated cost of Tk8,940 crore, of which the government is contributing Tk2,413 crore, with the remaining amount being financed by the investor consortium.
A separate project covers land acquisition, rehabilitation of affected people and consultancy services, with its entire cost borne by the government. The estimated cost of this component is Tk4,917 crore.
The combined estimated cost of the two projects stands at Tk13,857 crore.
The project was initiated in 2009, and the construction agreement was signed in 2011. The construction period was initially set at three and a half years, but the project could not be completed within the stipulated timeframe.

item.title: Dengue: 6 more die, 2,010 hospitalized in 24hrs
item.description:
Six more people died from dengue across the country in the 24 hours until 8:00am on Tuesday, while 2,010 new patients were hospitalised with the mosquito-borne disease.
The Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS) confirmed the figures in a press release issued on Tuesday.
Of the newly hospitalised patients, 943 were in Dhaka Division, 245 in Chittagong, 235 in Khulna, 219 each in Rajshahi and Barisal, 65 in Rangpur, 60 in Mymensingh and 24 in Sylhet.
Since the beginning of this year, a total of 140,909 people have been admitted to hospitals with dengue across the country, according to the DGHS.
Of them, 134,594 have recovered and been discharged, while 5,876 patients are currently receiving treatment at hospitals.
The dengue death toll this year has reached 439.

item.title: Exhibition marking Jail Killing Day postponed over security concerns
item.description:
The Liberation War Museum has postponed a special exhibition commemorating the four national leaders at the request of law enforcement agencies on Tuesday.
Mofidul Hoque, a trustee of the museum, said the decision to postpone the event was taken on Tuesday, following a request from law enforcement agencies citing security concerns.
The exhibition was scheduled to be inaugurated at 4pm on Tuesday at Gallery 6 on the museum's sixth floor. Waliul Islam, a former secretary who served in the wartime government, was scheduled to speak at the opening ceremony.
According to the invitation, the exhibition was organised to commemorate the contributions of the four national leaders, who played a significant role in the country's independence struggle and the Liberation War.
On November 3, 1975, the four leaders – Syed Nazrul Islam, acting president of the wartime Mujibnagar government; Tajuddin Ahmad, the country’s first prime minister; and cabinet members Captain M Mansur Ali and AHM Qamaruzzaman – who led Bangladesh's Liberation War, were killed inside Dhaka Central Jail.
The 15-day exhibition, titled “The Four National Leaders in the Independence Struggle,” was scheduled to run from November 3 to 17.
Officer-in-Charge of Sher-e-Bangla Nagar police station Monirul Islam told Dhaka Tribune that intelligence information had raised security concerns surrounding the event.
“After informing the organisers about the matter, they cancelled the programme,” he said.

item.title: World Bank: Bangladesh has two more decades to harness demographic dividend
item.description:
Bangladesh has roughly two decades before its working-age population share peaks in 2045, offering a crucial but temporary window to turn rapid demographic shifts into economic opportunity, according to a new World Bank report Tuesday.
While Bangladesh has more time than most of its regional peers, structural obstacles urgently require action, warns the report, titled Demographic Change in South Asia: From Tailwinds to Headwinds for Development .
Across South Asia, the working-age population numbering 1.17 billion people will peak and begin shrinking in less than 10 years.
By 2049, South Asia is projected to become an aged regional economy, with 14 percent of its population aged 65 and older. Bangladesh is expected to hit aged status in 2051.
Since 2000, an expanding share of prime-age adult workers has added 0.4% annually to South Asia's GDP and boosted labor productivity by 1.1% per year.
However, the region's demographic transition from an aging to an aged population is moving faster—and at lower per capita income levels—than in comparable emerging and developing economies.
As a result, the annual contribution of demographics to GDP growth is projected to shrink to just 0.1% between now and 2050.
“South Asian economies are aging faster and earlier in their development journeys,” said Johannes Zutt, World Bank vice president for South Asia.
“They need to act now to adopt policies and build infrastructure that create more and better jobs and deepen the gains from their ‘youth dividend’, while at the same time preparing for aging. This will enable South Asia to make the most of its large working age population and lay the foundations for a ‘second dividend’ as healthier older people continue contributing to the economy.”
The report highlights a persistent jobs gap in Bangladesh, where a favorable age structure has not fully translated into higher employment or productivity gains.
This shortfall is driven by limited formal job creation, low female labor-force participation, and lingering human capital gaps.
Approximately 84% of Bangladeshi workers—around 58 million people—are informally employed.
Higher education offers little guarantee of formal work, with 44% of university graduates holding informal jobs.
Furthermore, formal firms are expanding employment slowly, while small enterprises have, on average, shed workers recently.
“Bangladesh’s demographic opportunity depends on what it does now: help firms create better jobs, equip young people with market-relevant skills, and remove barriers that keep women out of work,” said Jean Pesme, World Bank division director for Bangladesh and Bhutan.
“At the same time, the country needs to start strengthening healthcare and old age income security for an aging population. That means meeting the growing financing need for aging transition will require stronger domestic resource mobilization.”
Systems for healthcare, long-term care, and pensions across South Asia remain poorly equipped for a population living longer without necessarily living healthier.
Currently, only 17% of the region's working-age population contributes to a pension scheme, and just 10% of older South Asians receive pension benefits—the lowest coverage rate worldwide.
To navigate this transition, the report recommends a dual strategy: sustaining the primary "youth dividend" by boosting job productivity, expanding MSME access to finance, streamlining regulations, enhancing education and health systems, and promoting female employment; and unlocking a "second dividend" through expanded healthcare, long-term care, pension safety nets, and increased national savings to raise long-term productivity.

item.title: Measles outbreak: Death toll reaches 1,263 as 6 die in 24hrs
item.description:
Six more children died with measles-like symptoms in the 24 hours ending at 8am on Tuesday, bringing the country’s combined tally of confirmed and suspected measles-related deaths to 1,263 this year.
The Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS) classified the latest fatalities as suspected measles deaths.
With this, the total number of suspected measles deaths has reached 1,158, while confirmed deaths have remained the same at 105.
A total of 1,318 new suspected measles cases were reported during the 24-hour period, taking the cumulative number of suspected cases nationwide to 232,823.
Meanwhile, 82 new confirmed measles cases were recorded, pushing laboratory-confirmed infections to 24,073.
Since March 15 this year, a total of 207,428 patients with suspected measles have been hospitalised across the country, of whom 198,752 have recovered, according to the DGHS.

item.title: HRFB expresses concern over sedition case against Satkhira rights activist
item.description:
Human Rights Forum Bangladesh (HRFB) has expressed deep concern over the filing of a sedition case against Shampa Goswami, executive director of Prerona Women Development Organisation in Satkhira, and fears that she may face further harassment and security risks.
According to information received from reliable sources, a case was filed against Shampa under Section 124A of the Bangladesh Penal Code at Shyamnagar police station in Satkhira on September 29, 2026.
Shampa has alleged that police surveillance is being conducted at her residence and her organisation’s office, while her family members are also being harassed.
In a statement, HRFB said allegations of this nature require particular consideration of the fundamental rights and privacy protections guaranteed by the Constitution of Bangladesh.
It noted that Article 36 of the Constitution guarantees citizens the right to freedom of movement, while Article 43 protects the privacy of the home and correspondence.
The organisation said allegations of surveillance at an individual's residence and workplace, as well as harassment of family members, must be treated with due seriousness.
HRFB also stressed that specific allegations are essential when bringing serious criminal charges, such as sedition, against individuals involved in human rights activities.
The forum called on the relevant authorities to examine the legal basis of the case against Shampa and verify the allegations, while also conducting an impartial investigation into the complaints she has raised.
It further urged the authorities to ensure that Shampa can continue her peaceful and legitimate human rights activities, including participating in international forums.
HRFB also called for appropriate measures to protect Shampa, her family members, and the staff and volunteers of the women's development organisation from intimidation, harassment or retaliatory action.
The statement was signed by Tahmina Rahman, convener of Human Rights Forum Bangladesh and executive director of Ain o Salish Kendra (ASK).

item.title: Workshop calls for evidence-based approach to tackling corruption
item.description:
A two-day national workshop on strengthening evidence-based approaches to measuring corruption and improving accountability in Bangladesh concluded at the Six Seasons Hotel in Gulshan-2, Dhaka, on Tuesday.
Titled “Measuring Corruption for Reform: Strengthening Evidence and Accountability in Bangladesh,” the workshop was jointly organised by the U4 Anti-Corruption Resource Centre, its partner embassies of Switzerland, Norway, the UK, Denmark and Germany, and the United Nations Office on Drugs and Crime (UNODC).
The workshop brought together government officials, development partners, academics, civil society representatives and international partners to strengthen Bangladesh’s capacity to monitor corruption trends and assess the impact of reform initiatives.
Over the two days, participants discussed international best practices, the operationalisation of the UNODC Statistical Framework to Measure Corruption, and ways to identify gaps, opportunities and priorities for improving corruption measurement and collaboration in Bangladesh.
Around 40 experts from relevant institutions reviewed existing data sources, including household surveys, administrative records and transparency assessments, to help build a comprehensive evidence base for ongoing national reforms.
The opening high-level session was attended by Anti-Corruption Commission Chairman Justice AKM Asaduzzaman as the chief guest.
In his speech, he stressed that sustainable anti-corruption reforms require collective commitment, adding that strong institutions, effective oversight, public participation and a culture of integrity are essential to building a society free from corruption.
Bangladesh Bureau of Statistics Director Md Emdadul Haque, who attended as a special guest, said the BBS remained committed to supporting national efforts to strengthen the evidence base for development and governance reforms within its mandate, and, where necessary, in collaboration with relevant institutions.
Swiss Ambassador to Bangladesh Reto Renggli said addressing corruption requires a collective shift in attitudes and mindsets, beginning in kindergartens and classrooms.
“Following rules is one thing, believing in the rules is a social precondition,” he said.
Norwegian Ambassador to Bangladesh Håkon Arald Gulbrandsen said Bangladesh would be among the first countries to implement the UNODC Statistical Framework to Measure Corruption if the initiative moves forward, describing it as a positive and practical step that would attract international attention.
UN Resident Coordinator a.i. Max Tunon underscored the strategic importance of measuring corruption and assessing the effectiveness of anti-corruption efforts for good governance, sustainable development and public trust in institutions.
He reaffirmed the UN system’s commitment to implementing the United Nations Convention against Corruption (UNCAC) and relevant resolutions of the Conference of the States Parties, particularly those related to corruption measurement.
He also stressed the importance of strengthening evidence-based public policies through the adoption of the UNODC statistical framework to demonstrate the actual impact of anti-corruption efforts in Bangladesh.
Transparency International Bangladesh (TIB) Executive Director Iftekharuzzaman highlighted the need to strengthen institutional capacity to generate credible corruption-related data.
“The problem in Bangladesh is often not so much the generation of data, as the lack of interest and commitment to use the available data and knowledge that already exist on corruption,” he said.
He also called for exploring innovative approaches to measuring the comparative implications of the multi-trillion-dollar global money-laundering economy for source and host economies.
Dr Sofie Schuette, principal adviser at the U4 Anti-Corruption Resource Centre at the Chr Michelsen Institute, and Shah Mohammad Naheeaan, head of office at UNODC, also attended the high-level session.
Schuette stressed the importance of data in driving reforms, saying credible evidence could help Bangladesh translate anti-corruption commitments into meaningful change by guiding reforms, strengthening accountability and making progress measurable.
The workshop concluded on Tuesday with panel reflections from representatives of key oversight bodies and development partners on establishing sustainable accountability mechanisms.

item.title: Clashes erupt in Mirpur for third consecutive day
item.description:
Clashes between police and garment workers erupted in Mirpur for the third consecutive day on Tuesday, disrupting traffic and prompting the temporary closure of Mirpur-11 metro station.
The clashes began around 10:15am when police intervened to prevent workers from blocking the road in the Mirpur-11 area, eyewitnesses said.
Workers intermittently emerged from side streets and hurled bricks and stones at police, who responded by firing tear gas shells and sound grenades to disperse them. The confrontation triggered repeated chases and counter-chases, leaving the area tense and traffic at a standstill.
Earlier in the morning, garment workers had left their factories and gathered outside their workplaces, with groups assembling along nearby side streets.
Yusuf Ahmed, a local resident and eyewitness, told Bangla Tribune that male and female workers from several factories between Mirpur-10 and Mirpur-11 had gathered outside their workplaces.
“Looking at the situation, it seems they could take to the main road at any moment,” he said.
Police remained on high alert as the situation developed.
Hafizur Rahman, officer-in-charge of Mirpur police station, said the situation in Mirpur-10 was normal.
“We remain on high alert, and any attempt to cause disorder will be met with strict action,” he said.
Garment workers have been protesting for some time, demanding a minimum monthly wage of Tk30,000. The protests turned violent on Sunday, when workers set fire to a police vehicle and clashed with law enforcement personnel.
Workers attempted to take to the streets again on Monday but were prevented from doing so by police.
According to a police source, around six people were arrested on Monday in connection with the unrest. Eleven cases have been filed over the clashes of the past two days, with more than 10,000 people named as accused.

item.title: Workers block Dhaka-Tangail highway, set fire to roadside waste in Gazipur
item.description:
Garment workers blocked the Dhaka-Tangail highway in Gazipur’s Naojor area on Tuesday, setting fire to roadside waste and bringing traffic to a standstill.
The blockade began around 9:30am in front of Diganta Sweater factory.
Workers dragged accumulated rubbish and waste from the roadside onto the highway and set it on fire, disrupting traffic between Joydebpur Chourasta and Naojor intersection.
Protesters also obstructed all vehicles, including auto-rickshaws and motorcycles. Some were seen playing cricket on the highway.
Journalists at the scene faced resistance from protesters when they attempted to speak to the workers and collect information, photographs and video footage.
Earlier in the morning, Mohammad Amjad Hossain, superintendent of Gazipur Industrial Police, said a group of workers had attempted to block the Dhaka-Tangail highway in the Mouchak area of Kaliakair shortly before 8am.
Law enforcement personnel intervened and persuaded the workers to clear the road without confrontation, he said, adding that security forces remained on high alert at several points along the highway.

item.title: BGB deployment in Gazipur increased to 11 platoons, magistrates to 25
item.description:
The administration has strengthened security in Gazipur amid ongoing garment workers’ protests over wage increases and other demands, deploying an additional platoon of Border Guard Bangladesh (BGB) personnel and increasing the number of executive magistrates.
The district now has 11 BGB platoons on duty, up from 10, while the number of executive magistrates has risen from 21 to 25.
Arif Hossain, assistant commissioner (media) at the Gazipur deputy commissioner’s office, confirmed the development on Tuesday morning.
He said BGB personnel were operating under the supervision of 25 executive magistrates, while other law enforcement agencies remained on high alert.
The additional deployment aims to prevent damage to public property and protect the lives and belongings of residents, he added.
Meanwhile, workers attempted to block the Dhaka-Tangail highway in Gazipur’s Mouchak area around 8:30am on Tuesday, but law enforcement personnel prevented them from occupying the road. Groups of workers were also seen heading to factories to join their shifts.
Mohammad Amjad Hossain, superintendent of Gazipur Industrial Police, said workers had attempted to block the highway shortly before 8am. Law enforcement personnel dispersed them, and traffic subsequently returned to normal.
For the past few days, garment workers in different parts of Gazipur have been staging protests over wage increases and other demands, blocking the Dhaka-Tangail and Dhaka-Mymensingh highways.
The unrest has involved incidents of arson, including fires at a police box, a police vehicle and a factory scrap warehouse. Clashes between workers and law enforcement personnel have also left people injured on both sides, while several individuals have been detained.
Several factories have suspended operations amid the protests.

PM calls for funding to support young innovators
item.description:
Prime Minister Tarique Rahman has called for ensuring that young people’s innovative ideas are not left unrealised because of a lack of funding.
“A single innovative idea from you could prove to be a game-changer for Bangladesh,” he said, adding that the government had allocated Tk500 crore annually for startups in the current budget.
He made the remarks while addressing the inauguration of a two-day Solar Expo as the chief guest on Tuesday morning at the Bangladesh-China Friendship Exhibition Centre in Agargaon, Dhaka.
The exhibition, themed “Utilize every inch of your rooftop and increase income through solar energy,” opened to visitors immediately after the inaugural ceremony. The prime minister also toured various stalls.
Power, Energy and Mineral Resources Minister Iqbal Hasan Mahmud presided over the event.
The prime minister said Bangladesh had previously become heavily dependent on imported energy, leaving the country vulnerable to disruptions in global supply chains caused by international conflicts.
To help stabilize the country's energy and power supply, the government had provided Tk43,000 crore in subsidies to the power sector in the 2025-26 fiscal year, he said.
He added that electricity demand remained at a similar level in the current fiscal year and that the government had increased its diesel reserves. Initiatives had also been taken to ensure adequate coal supplies for coal-fired power plants, while efforts to engage alternative suppliers were continuing.
The government had allocated Tk600 crore to procure fuel oil for electricity generation, he said.
Rather than spending time debating the failures or roles of previous governments in energy security and power generation, the government's priority was to meet future electricity demand and ensure an uninterrupted supply for households and businesses, he added.
He said the government was pursuing several initiatives simultaneously, including reviewing power-sector expenditure and contracts, intensifying domestic gas exploration, diversifying energy sources and rapidly expanding solar power generation.

item.title: Fresh clashes erupt as garment worker protests continue in Ashulia
item.description:
Ashulia’s industrial area remained tense on Tuesday as garment workers continued protesting for a minimum monthly wage of Tk30,000, extending unrest that has persisted for several days.
Intermittent clashes between workers and police began around 9am at several points along the Baipail-Abdullahpur road and continued through the morning.
Workers had initially arrived at factories for their shifts. However, after 8:30am, several factories, including a Hamim Group facility in Narsinghapur, suspended operations, prompting workers to take to the streets.
As workers gathered outside factories and attempted to block roads, police fired tear gas shells to disperse them.
During the confrontations, protesters also set fires at several locations in an attempt to block the road.
As of 11:20am, the situation remained tense in Nishchintapur and the Unique area along the Baipail-Abdullahpur road.
Although police dispersed the protesters using tear gas and charges, workers later regrouped in nearby alleyways.
Sources said several factory authorities had been forced to suspend operations amid the unrest, but the exact number of affected factories was not immediately known.

item.title: E-immigration launched at Shahjalal airport arrival counters, easing passenger hassle
item.description:
An automated border control system, or e-gate, has been introduced at the arrival counters of Hazrat Shahjalal International Airport in Dhaka, allowing e-passport holders to complete immigration in just 18 to 20 seconds and avoid long queues.
The introduction of e-gates at the arrivals section has eased passenger hassle and significantly reduced the time required for immigration, officials said.
Speaking to Dhaka Tribune on Monday afternoon, Department of Immigration and Passports (DIP) Director General Major General Md Alimul Amin said e-gates had been introduced at the airport’s arrival counters and passengers could now complete immigration within a very short time.
“We also want to introduce e-gate services at departures. We are working on it,” he said.
However, he said the departure service was not yet technically ready. Although passengers’ passports can be scanned at the departure e-gates, the system cannot currently complete the required stamping process, leaving the service suspended.
During a visit to the airport, a Dhaka Tribune correspondent found that passengers still have to collect their arrival stickers manually from a police booth after completing e-immigration.
Officials said the process would be simplified once the third terminal becomes operational, and passengers would no longer have to visit the police booth separately to collect their arrival stickers.
Airport immigration officials said Bangladesh faces several technical and operational challenges in fully digitising immigration services, including e-gates and e-visa verification.
These challenges include an insufficient number of e-gates and barcode and biometric reader devices, frequent server downtime and delays in IT systems.
There is also no real-time integration among the databases of the National Identity Card (NID) system, the Department of Immigration and Passports (DIP) and the Bureau of Manpower, Employment and Training (BMET).
As a result, even minor discrepancies in passengers’ names or dates of birth can prevent e-gates from automatically identifying them.
Technical problems with facial-recognition cameras and fingerprint-matching systems can also cause the gates to reject legitimate passengers. In addition, some immigration officials lack the technical expertise needed to operate digital systems and verify e-visas.
Major General Alimul Amin said several technical, institutional and practical challenges remain in converting departure immigration into a fully digital system.
“That is why the service is currently suspended. But we are working to simplify this service, as well as passport-related services, as soon as possible,” he said.
Passengers said the introduction of e-gates at arrivals had reduced both waiting time and hassle, allowing them to complete immigration automatically within 18 to 20 seconds.
Liton Kabir, who recently returned from Thailand, told Dhaka Tribune: “The e-passport was once a dream for the people of Bangladesh. The e-gate was introduced alongside it. Although the service was closed for various reasons, I feel relieved now that it has reopened. If it is introduced at departures soon, travelling will become even easier.”
Rajib Ahmed, who recently returned from Turkey, said the service had made the arrival process much easier.
“This was our first family tour. With an e-passport, you can clear immigration in about 18 seconds. It would have been great to have the facility at departures too, as it would save a lot of time. The government should pay attention to this,” he said.
An immigration official said passengers using e-gates at departures still have to return to the immigration desk for visa verification and other checks, meaning the process takes almost as long as before.
“This makes passengers angry. Data from the e-gates also often fails to reach the immigration software. That is why the departure e-gates have remained closed,” he said.
He added that while e-gates are currently closed for departing passengers at Shahjalal Airport, they are operational for arriving passengers.
Bangladesh introduced e-passports in February 2020, becoming the first country in South Asia to do so. E-gates were subsequently installed at Hazrat Shahjalal International Airport to facilitate faster and more efficient immigration processing.
However, technical problems and the continued need for manual visa verification and other checks created complications. As a result, passengers still had to visit immigration desks even after using the e-gates, prompting authorities to suspend their operation.
Several members of the Immigration Police's Special Branch, speaking on condition of anonymity, said around 40% of passengers using the airport each day hold e-passports.
They said the e-gates can automatically verify passport and passenger information but cannot independently verify visas.
The system also lacks provisions to automatically store information on passengers’ destinations or flights.
Consequently, visa verification continues to be conducted manually, even when passengers use the e-gates. This contributes to long queues at departure immigration, particularly when several flights arrive or depart around the same time.
Hazrat Shahjalal International Airport Executive Director Group Captain SM Ragib Samad told Dhaka Tribune that the e-gates can currently verify only passport information and cannot verify visas and other details.
“That is why the e-gates have been kept closed at departures. But we hope the service will start soon,” he said.
The government has taken an initiative to modernise Bangladesh's immigration system by integrating the existing Immigration Management System (IMS) with new technologies.
The Ministry of Home Affairs has formed a 10-member committee to review fee-setting, payment collection and settlement procedures under the system and develop an appropriate financial model.
The notice was issued on October 19 by the Departure-4 branch of the ministry's Security Services Division and published on October 25.
According to the notice, the government plans to integrate the Advance Passenger Information System (APIS), Passenger Name Record (PNR), e-Visa and Electronic Travel Authorisation (ETA) systems, as well as a sovereign data analytics platform, with the existing IMS.
The government is also considering appointing a third party to modernise the relevant infrastructure and implement the programme. As part of the initiative, the committee will review immigration facilitation charges, revenue collection and remittance procedures, and payment mechanisms. It will also prepare proposals on appropriate fees and a suitable financial model.
The committee is headed by the Joint Secretary of the Planning-1 wing of the Ministry of Home Affairs, while the Deputy Secretary of the Departure-4 branch will serve as its member-secretary.
Other members include the Joint Secretary of the Departure-1 wing of the Home Ministry and representatives from the Finance Division, National Board of Revenue (NBR), Civil Aviation Authority of Bangladesh (CAAB), Special Branch, Biman Bangladesh Airlines, Bangladesh Land Port Authority and the Department of Immigration and Passports.

item.title: LPG price hiked again, 12kg cylinder now Tk2,060
item.description:
The Bangladesh Energy Regulatory Commission (BERC) has raised liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) prices by Tk223 per 12kg cylinder, setting the new price at Tk2,060 amid an ongoing supply shortage.
The price was previously Tk1,837. The price of autogas has also increased from Tk84.62 to Tk91.95 per litre.
The revised prices will take effect at 8:00pm on Monday, BERC said.
Prices have been raised across all cylinder sizes, ranging from 5kg to 45kg.
BERC last raised the price of a 12kg LPG cylinder by Tk252 on October 4, from Tk1,585 to Tk1,837. The latest hike comes just a month later, amid ongoing supply shortages and complaints of higher market prices.
On October 29, BERC held a public hearing on LPG prices and proposed increases in storage, bottling and distribution charges. During the hearing, LPG operators, distributors and retailers placed separate proposals for raising their charges.
Operators proposed increasing bottling charges from Tk15–16 to Tk25–30 per kg. They also sought to raise distribution charges from Tk4.17 to Tk8.33 per kg and retail charges from Tk3.75 to Tk10 per kg.
Distributors proposed increasing their charge on each 12kg cylinder from Tk50 to Tk150, while retailers sought to raise theirs from Tk45 to Tk70.
After reviewing the proposals, BERC's technical evaluation committee recommended raising the price of a 12kg cylinder from Tk1,837 to Tk1,976, an increase of Tk139.
Following the hearing, the commission set November 2 as the deadline for submitting opinions on the proposals. It announced the revised prices on the final day for receiving feedback.
